## Targets and complete telescopes

Every target has the section binders implicit `{G : Type u}`, `[Group G]`
and `[TopologicalSpace G]`, with the single universe parameter `u`, followed
by the explicit and instance binders shown. The normality binder
`[hLnormal : (L.toSubgroup.subgroupOf K.field.toSubgroup).Normal]` is the
source binder `[hLnormal : (extensionSubgroup K.field L hLK).Normal]` with
the source abbreviation `extensionSubgroup` (M004.002) expanded to its exact
Mathlib body, as in the sibling Definitions module; likewise the finiteness
binder of M014.039. Write `G_K` for `K.field.toSubgroup`, `G_L` for
`L.toSubgroup.subgroupOf K.field.toSubgroup`, `G(\widetilde L|K)` for the
quotient `K.field.toSubgroup ⧸ D.extensionInertiaWithin K.field L hLK`, and
`Γ` for the closed subgroup `D.frobeniusClosure K L hLK σ` of
`G(\widetilde L|K)` topologically generated by the Frobenius lift `σ`.

```lean
def frobeniusExponent_posStatement (D : DegreeData G) (K : FiniteResidueAbstractField D) (L :
  ClosedSubgroup G)
    (hLK : L.toSubgroup ≤ K.field.toSubgroup)
    [hLnormal : (L.toSubgroup.subgroupOf K.field.toSubgroup).Normal]
    (σ : D.FrobeniusElements K L hLK) : Prop :=
    0 < D.frobeniusExponent K L hLK σ
```

The natural number `d_K(σ)` chosen for the Frobenius lift `σ` is strictly
positive.

```lean
def extensionNormalizedDegree_frobenius_eq_powStatement (D : DegreeData G)
    (K : FiniteResidueAbstractField D) (L : ClosedSubgroup G)
    (hLK : L.toSubgroup ≤ K.field.toSubgroup)
    [hLnormal : (L.toSubgroup.subgroupOf K.field.toSubgroup).Normal]
    (σ : D.FrobeniusElements K L hLK) : Prop :=
    D.extensionNormalizedDegree K L hLK σ.1 =
      (Multiplicative.ofAdd (1 : ZHat)) ^
          D.frobeniusExponent K L hLK σ
```

The normalized degree of the underlying element `σ.1 ∈ G(\widetilde L|K)` is
the `d_K(σ)`-th power of the multiplicative generator `ofAdd 1`, that is,
`d_K(σ) · 1` in `ZHat`.

```lean
def frobeniusInClosure_topologicallyGeneratesStatement
    (D : DegreeData G) [IsTopologicalGroup G]
    (K : FiniteResidueAbstractField D) (L : ClosedSubgroup G)
    (hLK : L.toSubgroup ≤ K.field.toSubgroup)
    [hLnormal : (L.toSubgroup.subgroupOf K.field.toSubgroup).Normal]
    (σ : D.FrobeniusElements K L hLK) : Prop :=
    TopologicallyGenerates
      ({D.frobeniusInClosure K L hLK σ} : Set
        (D.frobeniusClosure K L hLK σ))
```

Inside the topological group `Γ` (with the subspace topology and the instance
M014.025), the singleton consisting of `σ` regarded as an element of `Γ`
topologically generates `Γ`: the closure of the subgroup it generates is all
of `Γ`.

```lean
def frobeniusClosure_totallyDisconnectedSpaceStatement (D : DegreeData G)
    [IsTopologicalGroup G] [CompactSpace G] [T2Space G]
    [TotallyDisconnectedSpace G]
    (K : FiniteResidueAbstractField D) (L : ClosedSubgroup G)
    (hLK : L.toSubgroup ≤ K.field.toSubgroup)
    [hLnormal : (L.toSubgroup.subgroupOf K.field.toSubgroup).Normal]
    (σ : D.FrobeniusElements K L hLK) : Prop :=
    TotallyDisconnectedSpace (D.frobeniusClosure K L hLK σ)
```

When `G` is a compact, Hausdorff, totally disconnected topological group,
`Γ` with its subspace topology is totally disconnected.

```lean
def frobeniusFixedField_finiteIndexStatement (D : DegreeData G)
    [IsTopologicalGroup G] [CompactSpace G] [T2Space G]
    (K : FiniteResidueAbstractField D) (L : ClosedSubgroup G)
    (hLK : L.toSubgroup ≤ K.field.toSubgroup)
    [hLnormal : (L.toSubgroup.subgroupOf K.field.toSubgroup).Normal]
    [hLfinite : Finite (K.field.toSubgroup ⧸ L.toSubgroup.subgroupOf K.field.toSubgroup)]
    (σ : D.FrobeniusElements K L hLK) : Prop :=
    Finite
      ((K.field.toSubgroup ⧸ D.extensionInertiaWithin K.field L hLK) ⧸
        (D.frobeniusClosure K L hLK σ).toSubgroup)
```

When `G` is a compact Hausdorff topological group and `G_L` has finite index
in `G_K`, the coset space of `G(\widetilde L|K)` modulo the subgroup
underlying `Γ` is finite, that is, `Γ` has finite index in
`G(\widetilde L|K)`. This is the Galois-dual form of the finiteness of the
fixed field `Σ` of `Γ` over `K`. The hypothesis `hLfinite` is used only by
the source proof.

Binder order and kinds are those of the source theorems. No target has any
further hypothesis.
